leads.title: Obergefell v. Hodges - U.S. Supreme Court decision
leads.documents: Legalizes same-sex marriage in North Dakota since June 26, 2015; found denial of marriage rights to same-sex couples unconstitutional, overriding state Constitution and statute limiting marriage to one man-one woman.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as June 26, 2015 decision

leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County, consolidated with Altitude Express, Inc. v. Zarda and R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes Inc. v. EEOC - U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Establishes workplace discrimination on basis of sexual orientation or gender identity is discrimination on basis of sex under Title VII, protecting LGBT employees despite lack of explicit North Dakota statute.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as June 15, 2020 ruling

leads.title: Ramsay v. Dalrymple - federal lawsuit
leads.documents: Challenge to North Dakota's refusal to license and recognize same-sex marriages; initiated June 2014, proceedings suspended January 2015 pending U.S. Supreme Court action in related cases.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited with case name and dates June 2014 / January 2015

leads.title: Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act - U.S. federal law
leads.documents: Provides federal prosecution avenue for hate crimes based on sexual orientation or gender identity in North Dakota, where state hate-crime law does not cover those categories; signed 2009 by President Barack Obama.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as 2009 federal law

leads.title: Federal Hate Crimes Statistics Act of 1990
leads.documents: Encouraged states to report hate crime data to FBI; article notes Fargo is city responsible for reporting to state and federal governments and that studies show 2 in 3 hate crimes go unreported.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as 1990 Act

leads.title: North Dakota Legislature - gender-affirming care ban for minors
leads.documents: Makes it illegal to provide gender-affirming care to minors; passed by veto-proof majority April 5, 2023.
leads.detail: No URL or bill number visible in text; cited as April 5, 2023 veto-proof passage

leads.title: North Dakota Legislature - transgender sports bans and 2021 veto
leads.documents: 2021 bill to ban transgender girls from girls school sports passed House 69-25 and Senate 27-20, vetoed April 21, 2021 by Gov. Doug Burgum; April 2023 pair of bills signed banning AMAB transgender individuals from female sports in schools and higher education.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited with vote counts and veto/signing dates

leads.title: North Dakota Legislature - bathroom restriction and pronoun/outing laws, identity documents rule
leads.documents: April 2023 bathroom law restricting transgender public bathroom usage in many state-run facilities effective July 1; May law forbidding schools/government entities from requiring or prohibiting preferred pronouns and requiring outing to parents effective July 1; May 2023 birth certificate gender-change restriction and DOT driver license rule requiring physician/therapist letter of permanent gender role transition.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as March/May/April 2023 legislative actions, veto of earlier pronoun ban, effective July 1

leads.title: Human Rights Campaign - Municipal Equality Index
leads.documents: Documents city-level non-discrimination machinery: Fargo policy since 2001 for city employees covering sexual orientation, Jamestown similar policy, Grand Forks June 17, 2013 protections for city employees/applicants and later rental housing ban; added Bismarck and Mandan in 2016, removed in later versions.
